summary: Build scoring models, benefits maps, and governance dashboards to prioritize portfolios with confidence and prove value.
lede: Digital portfolio prioritization and benefits realization help you compare initiatives consistently, make defensible trade-offs, and connect investment choices to strategic outcomes. This course provides practical methods for weighted scoring, dependency analysis, capacity balancing, benefits mapping, and governance decision-making. Build portfolio scorecards, initiative registers, realization trackers, and decision logs to bring structure to complex choices. You will also practice scenario-based trade-off analysis and learn how to re-prioritize initiatives when budget, capacity, risk, dependencies, or strategic priorities change.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who evaluate, govern, or report on competing initiatives and need a practical method for portfolio choices and benefits tracking. Portfolio Managers who balance demand, value, risk, and delivery capacity. PMO Analysts who maintain portfolio registers and scoring matrices. Transformation Managers who sequence digital initiatives against strategic priorities. Benefits Realization Managers who track planned and actual outcome measures. Program Managers who escalate trade-offs and dependency conflicts. Strategy Managers who translate investment choices into enterprise priorities. Business Case Authors who define benefits, costs, and assumptions. Finance Business Partners who review portfolio funding and value cases. Enterprise Architects who assess initiative dependencies and sequencing impacts. Governance Leads who prepare portfolio decisions for executive review.
prerequisites: Participants should have working familiarity with project, program, or portfolio environments and a basic understanding of business cases, governance forums, and benefits tracking. Experience with portfolio registers, spreadsheet-based scoring models, or PMO reporting is helpful. No coding is required, although comfort with data tables, dashboards, and structured decision templates will improve the learning experience. The course is taught at an intermediate level, with advanced concepts such as portfolio analytics and automated reporting introduced at operational depth.
